subject: Logging provenance & onboarding checklist for Streamline Health RFP

From: Elaine Turner <elaine.turner@streamlinehealth.com>

Cc: procurement@streamlinehealth.com

Subject: Quick clarifications on audit log export / chain-of-custody

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the RFP materials last week. A couple of quick follow-ups from our security and legal teams as we build the evaluation checklist: could you confirm the following about Redwood's audit logging and exportability?

1) Retention windows: what are your default retention windows for admin/audit logs vs request-level traces in the hosted product, and do you offer configurable retention per-tenant for Dedicated/Private?

2) Export formats & APIs: do you provide a bulk export API that can produce time-bound bundles (e.g., a 30-day slice) in a machine-parsable format? What formats are supported (NDJSON, CSV, parquet)?

3) Immutability & provenance: for compliance we need to demonstrate that exported records are tamper-evident. Do you produce signed snapshots or checksums for exported bundles? Any chain-of-custody guidance?

4) For legal holds/eDiscovery: what is the turnaround SLA to produce a preservation snapshot for a single customer (including metadata, request/response bodies, and redaction notes)?

If you can share a short playbook or example schema for exports that would be really helpful. We appreciate concise answers — our procurement deadline is 8/5.

Best,
Elaine Turner
Head of Security & Compliance
Streamline Health

--
Elaine Turner
Streamline Health | elaine.turner@streamlinehealth.com
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on audit log export / chain-of-custody

Hi Elaine — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (tech lead, Evidence & Exports) and Rishi (legal/security) to provide the concrete details and attach our export playbook. High level answers below; Marissa/Rishi will add specifics and the artifacts you asked for.

1) Retention windows: Hosted default: 90 days for request-level traces, 365 days for admin/audit events (configurable tiers available). Dedicated: retention is configurable per contract — we commonly offer 30/90/365 options, plus custom longer-term archival. Private: customer-managed retention by default; Redwood can enable policy enforcement if requested.

2) Export formats & APIs: we provide a time-bound bulk export API that can stream NDJSON or Parquet, and a CSV schema for summary exports. Exports are delivered as compressed bundles (gz) with a manifest.

3) Immutability & provenance: we include SHA256 checksums for each file in the bundle manifest; for Dedicated/Private we can also produce signed manifests (PKI) on request. We document the provenance (server id, region, kernel timestamps) in metadata fields.

4) Legal hold SLA: standard hosted SLA is 5 business days for a full preservation snapshot; expedited 48-hour for paid emergency requests. For Dedicated/Private we can negotiate faster SLAs as part of the contract.

Attaching a playbook and a sample schema — Marissa will confirm the field-level mappings and Rishi will confirm legal language.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Elaine / Kimberly — adding the technical details and examples below, pasted from the playbook. Sharing the sample CSV/NDJSON schema as requested (attached in next email).

- Export slice semantics: exports accept start_ts and end_ts (ISO8601). We guarantee inclusion of all events with server_timestamp >= start_ts and < end_ts. For high-throughput customers we also provide chunked export pagination with stable cursors.

- Schema highlights (example fields): event_id, server_timestamp, tenant_id, request_id, user_id (if applicable), endpoint, request_body_sha256, response_body_sha256, auth_context (role, token_id), action_type, resource_path, sample_trust_score. The CSV sample includes normalized columns; NDJSON includes full nested payloads.

- Checksums & signing: each exported file has a file-level SHA256; the manifest lists file_name, byte_size, sha256, and earliest_ts/latest_ts in the bundle. For Dedicated we can produce a PKCS7-signed manifest and an optional chain-of-custody PDF that records the export operator, job id, and TLS fingerprint.

- Tamper evidence recommendations: maintain the bundle manifest in your own archive and verify SHA256 post-transfer. For legal matters we recommend storing the manifest in an immutable storage (S3 Object Lock) or in your internal evidence ledger.

- Redaction notes: we support redaction markers in the export for PII fields (redacted_by_job_id, redaction_policy_version). Redaction is applied during export when requested; original raw logs are retained per retention policy and subject to governance.

Next steps: I'll send the actual CSV/NDJSON sample files and a short script showing how to verify the manifest checksum against a local copy.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Tech Lead, Evidence & Exports
